description: Two-panel composite of back-scattered/greyscale SEM micrographs of the same alloy, Fe–22Mn–0.4C–1.5Al–1.5Si (wt%) steel produced by metal injection molding (MIM) and sintered at 1360 °C. (a) is the 1 h sintered condition: a fully austenitic matrix of equiaxed, polygonal grains with straight, mutually impinging boundaries, each grain internally crossed by fine parallel striations/etch lines; dark, rounded manganese oxide particles sit on and along the grain boundaries and in small clusters, with white arrows labelling "Manganese oxide" (dark particles) and "austenitic matrix" (the light-toned grains). A scale bar at lower right reads 200 μm. (b) is the 3 h sintered condition at the same magnification and identical 200 μm scale bar: grain size is visibly coarser, the dark manganese oxide particles form a more continuous, thicker network along the grain boundaries, and the intragranular striations are more pronounced and better resolved. Together the two panels argue that longer sintering at 1360 °C coarsens the austenitic matrix while leaving and redistributing the manganese oxide second phase along the grain boundaries, i.e. that the MIM + sintering route yields a fully austenitic structure with grain-boundary manganese oxide particles, consistent with the caption.

subfigures.description: Greyscale SEM micrograph of Fe–22Mn–0.4C–1.5Al–1.5Si (wt%) MIM steel sintered at 1360 °C for 1 h. Equiaxed polygonal austenitic grains with fine internal striations; dark rounded manganese oxide particles at grain boundaries and in clusters; arrows label 'Manganese oxide' (dark particles) and 'austenitic matrix'. Scale bar 200 μm at lower right.

Same alloy and modality, sintered at 1360 °C for 3 h. Coarser equiaxed austenitic grains with clearer internal striations; dark manganese oxide particles form a thicker, more continuous grain-boundary network. Same 'Manganese oxide' and 'austenitic matrix' labels with white arrows and the same 200 μm scale bar.

observations.observation: Both panels are greyscale SEM micrographs of the same alloy, Fe–22Mn–0.4C–1.5Al–1.5Si (wt%), with an identical 200 μm scale bar printed at the lower right of each panel.
White arrows in each panel label two features by name: dark rounded particles annotated 'Manganese oxide' and the light polygonal grains annotated 'austenitic matrix'.
The matrix consists of equiaxed, polygonal grains separated by straight boundaries, with fine parallel striations visible inside individual grains.
The manganese oxide second phase appears as dark, rounded particles concentrated along the grain boundaries, with some clustered agglomerates.
Panel (b) (3 h sinter) shows visibly coarser grains and a thicker, more continuous grain-boundary manganese oxide network than panel (a) (1 h sinter) at the same magnification.
The caption states panel (a) corresponds to sintering at 1360 °C for 1 h and panel (b) to 1360 °C for 3 h.
The caption states the material is Fe–22Mn–0.4C–1.5Al–1.5Si (wt%) steel processed by MIM (metal injection molding).
The caption describes the figure as microstructure and notes it is adapted with permission from a 2019 Taylor & Francis Group publication (ref. 91).
The citing text states the steel powder was combined with high-density polyethylene (HDPE) and paraffin wax (PW) for mixing and immersed in solvent, then sintered at 1200–1360 °C.
The citing text states the sintering is employed to obtain a fully austenitic structure with equally distributed manganese oxide particles, matching the two labelled features in the micrographs.
The citing text proposes that, following this fabrication method, ultrahard SiC, alumina and nitride particles can be mixed into the steel powder to further improve wear resistance.
No quantitative grain-size or particle-size values are printed in either panel; only the 200 μm scale bar and the two text labels are present.
